11758.d:
This project started as a way to teach myself more about classes in p5.js by trying to code the "Chaos Game" method of plotting a Serpinski Triangle

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kbKtFN71Lfs

Once figured out, I expanded the method to other shapes to see if different types of fractals might form. They did not, but the result was a series of points that could be connected with thin lines to draw shapes without using the native functions of p5. After working on colors it seemed like a nice enough project to release for free to everyone. Thank you all for your interest and support, hope you get a cool one!

11760.d:
Idea of Hauntology is referring to the return or persistence of elements from the social or cultural past, as in the manner of a ghost.

This implies a contemporary culture's persistent recycling of retro aesthetics and a sense of nostalgia for the lost futures.

Flowers and herbaceous plants are short-lived creatures, but when dried, in herbarium mode, they can be stored much longer and ensure the repetition of the stories associated with them.
Therefore, special conditions must be created for the existence of ghosts. These conditions are usually created by people, and sometimes people themselves become these very conditions.

Artwork is based on PNG layers (with masks), Disco Diffusion, python and p5.js code.

11762.d:
The Hansup genesis on fxhash. :)

Hash_people simply places all characters of the fxhash in a tight grid and set in a custom font (HSP1). Only some characters have bright colors: there is a red cat, blue dogs, an orange rabbit, a yellow Hansup, purple and green robots, white numbers and the grey zero.

With a keyboard you can do the following:
H-key toggle freezes the random animation of the white numbers. The numbers from the fxhash are displayed.
SPACEBAR / mouse click / touch toggle makes the characters run through the whole grid. 
S-key toggle is for sorting the characters 
R-key toggle is for reversing the order of the characters
F-key toggles fullscreen
P-key saves the canvas. You might want the freeze (H-key) first to pause the random number animation  and capture all the fxhash characters.

Folding and cutting papers was one of my favorite papercraft activities in my childhood. Even when I grew up, I continued to use papercutting as a fun activity with my nieces to cut even more interesting shapes and push the limits of our imaginations.

In Papercut Factory, I tried to translate those memories into code, and as a result, into generative art, by creating an almost infinite number of variations.

The use of different shapes, color and quality of paper, varying grids, cut zones, random cut shapes, sizes and positions, background style and color resulted in millions or even billions of possible unique outcomes.

I hope that you will find something beautiful from your childhood in Papercut Factory 🤗

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one more traveled by,
A hash then made all the difference
~ Robert Frost (very nearly)

In these woods paths each begin from a single source. Individuals start at that source and branch outwards.
At each branching step, an individual may elect to go in any available direction, but has a bias towards paths that have been more heavily traveled previously.
Paths are shaded according to how much traffic they've received.
Obstacles may be added, resulting in distinctive growth patterns.

Features
grid mode: In which directions can we branch
arrangement: Where are paths and obstacles situated
palette: What colors are used
lighting: Light mode or dark mode

Keyboard:
'a': Animate your creation
'l': Toggle light mode

11805.d:
Inspired by traditional Japanese wagami design. We use the iconic patterns of our previous projects to recreate this artwork. All the patterns are generated first and then used to build the scene. 

In this project Aluan brings his delicate texture from his 'Chaos' series, Jinyao brings his beloved pattern from the 'Cloud' series and Wen brings his iconic pattern from the 'Maze'. 'Collage' is not just about mixing our style, but it is also about finding harmony among all the elements. 'Collage' is also about working together, in that we can create something that's difficult to achieve or imagine if we were working alone.

Each piece contains the patterns of all the 3 artists, each artist has a certain number of patterns with different colors. Depending which artist you get, his pattern will be shown as the primary color theme while the pattern of the other 2 artists turns into grayscale to make the primary pattern with color stand out. 

There are 7 different scenes included in this project, which are : Mountains, Waves, Lake, Hexagons, Tetrapods, Chrysanthemums and Lotus. We took great inspiration from the traditional Japanese design, and we discovered these are some of the most common elements in it. Therefore we decide to use them and reimagine them by mixing our patterns. 

The title 'Collage' doesn't only apply to the visual style, but also to the code as well. In this project we mixed p5.js and Vanilla JS. While Aluan and Jinyao work with their patterns in p5. Wen gathered the patterns and recreated the full scene in Vanilla JS.

It is not difficult to imagine the reason why we form this collaboration is because we are all Taiwanese. However we are all based in different cities or even different countries. In this journey we learned about each other's style, inspirations and ways of working. We learn that despite the time and location difference, we have a lot in common. And one of the biggest things we all have in common is our love for this land and the people of Taiwan. Therefore we decided to donate 25% of the income from this project to the FAB DAO ( Formosa Art Bank.)
FAB DAO is a non-profit organisation based in Taiwan that focuses on building a community that includes the features of charity, culture, and art by organising and selling non-profit NFTs. FAB DAO directs its advocacy towards minting non-profit NFTs, supporting artists in getting involved in web3, and providing blockchain education services.

Kinetics is a neo-constructivist generative art project by Andrew Mitchell, built in p5js.

 * CLICK TO PAUSE.
 * Increase and decrease the p5js framerate by tapping the left and right arrows.
 * Pause the top layer by tapping down arrow.
 * Save a frame by tapping S (works when opened in it's own tab).
 * Press H for High Quality, M for Default, L for Low Quality. Note, this effects performance.
 * Reset the Kinetic by by tapping backspace.

Each Kinetic delicately moves from it's origin, giving the appearance of infinite space and possibility. The viewer witnesses the construction of the Kinetic floating inside of the negative. Shapes and lines move around the Kinetic in a dazzling display of contrasting color.

The texture developed for Kinetics, deemed The Creation of the Universe (See top right) is at its core a color gradient of 3 different colors. Each piece construct's itself, drawing lines on top of lines to create a unique self contained assembly of materials as opposed to a realistic abstraction. The Creation of the Universe repeats itself in each piece, just as cells do in an organic structure. From here is where it initially got it's name.

Inspired heavily by the works of Rodchenko and Tatlin, each Kinetic appears to slot together like a puzzle. Each piece has multiple hard edge planes clashing aggressively with each other giving the sense that there is more than just a flat canvas. A quasi realism is created through our desire to build instead of simply paint.

"Long Live Generative Art"

- Mitchell

"estruturas.14" is my first project using the p5js library for generative art.

The aesthetic concept that I attempted to translate onto the canvas was the formation of interconnected points that form structures. fxrand is used to set the position, dot/dash size, movement pattern, and canvas position at random. This randomization is also reflected in the color palettes used.

The vibrating movement and the structure's movement were designed to give the impression of something alive. It's like a mechanism. We are connected to the structure by a combination of interactive movement, point connections, and vibration.

Composition

- 22 pallets, each with 5 colors

- Background color: white or black

- fxrand determines the grayscale using square or ellipse orbs.

- 5 - 20 "estruturas"

Interactivity

- To coordinate the movement of the "estruturas," press and drag the mouse left button; 

- To coordinate movement and orb size, press and drag the scroll button.

- To return "estruturas" to its original position, press T; to stop the return movement, press P.

- To save a png file, press S.

This code is licenced with CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/

Special thanks to everyone who assisted me in getting in touch with this new library and, as a result, with a new set of possibilities.

11858.d:
This system is a composite of two generative layers: and invisible force field, and a swarm of particles that move around and leave an inky trail on the screen. There are only two forces at play: gravity towards the center, and repulsion between the particles, which becomes more or less strong depending on the underlying force field. In other words, it is like the particles “shrink” or “grow” depending on their position.
These simple conditions create emergent behavior with most particles moving in loops, analogous to convective cells in a fluid with heterogeneous densities. 
Press [m] to show the particles and see the system dynamics more clearly. You can also double click/tap anywhere on the screen to move the center of gravity and generate a different drawing from the same force field. 

This script will adapt nicely to any screen size and ratio.

Controls:
[SPACE] to play/pause
[Double click / tap] to relocate the center of gravity
[r] to recenter gravity and restart the drawing
[m] to toggle between path drawing and particle swarm views
[i] to reveal the hidden force field
[s] to download capture
[f] to toggle fullscreen
[2] to [9] to generate and save a hi-res image at 2x, 3x, … your viewport size (wait for the drawing to finish – might take longer at higher resolutions)

Made with p5.js.

3D funicular structure + Rope true physics + Optical illusions

A very humble tribute to Antoni Gaudi's amazing work with funicular structures (used for the fabulous Sagrada Familia in Barcelona) in virtual interactive 3D with true rope physics simulation and some fun mirroring effects.

This genius architect was inspired by nature, its shapes and laws. He was using an empirical technique called "funicular structure" to model his building by hanging ropes with weights from a ceiling. When gravity made it stable, he could put a big mirror below and watch what it would look like on the ground. Then he could report this structure bottom to top and later, it was mathematically proven that this approach was legit.

This is a new platform of work for me so if you like this work, stay tuned for more experimentations later!

WARNING: Webgl/GPU advised, CPU/mobile compliant but might lag.

Controls:
- H: hide/show help.
- Dbl-Click - Space: start/pause animation for snapshots.
- I: hide/show info panel. Click for panels (info, FPS).

Gaudi's Funicular @naibdian 2022 using Opensource WebGL, ThreeJS libs, AmmoJS, CirclePacker by Georg Fischer, NVIDIA FXAA anti-aliasing shader by Timothy Lottes.

11873.d:
‘Anom Nos’ is a series of abstract works based around one of the world's most famous noses. Each piece in the Anom Nos series will be generated by drawing upon 486 unique PNG elements. Each of these elements is pre-made and has been organised unevenly across 39 different layers.

When a piece is generated, it will take one element from each of these 39 layers. There is an equal probability for each of the PNG elements across 38 of these layers - who nose what might appear! The final layer, however, is where the magic happens. It is in this layer that the nose elements are located.

In the final layer you will be rewarded with either a: Rainbow(1), Gold(2), Red(5), Green(10), Pink(15), Blue(20) or Grey(30) nose. The number after each of the nose colors above, is the likelihood of receiving one. For example: A chance of 5 (Red nose) is half as likely to appear as a chance of 10 (Green Nose), but five times as likely as a chance of 1 (Rainbow Nose). Basically, the lower the number, the rarer your nose. Rainbow noses are the most rare, Grey noses are the least.

Creator Notes:
* Each possible PNG element is a 100% original creation of the artist. The code used to make these elements come together is by the genius and generous @PureSpider.
* CC BY-NC-ND 4.0

There was an equal probability for each of the PNG elements across 38 of the layers. In the final layer, however, a nose was selected with unequal probability. The rarity of noses (from most to least rare) is as follows: Rainbow, Gold, Red, Green, Pink, Blue, Grey.

My journey with line art, discovering the state space of patterns created by simple lines lined up or crossing each other, started in late 2012, with developing a multi-touch iPad drawing/creativity app called TwoToJazz. What writing generative code since early 2022 has allowed me is to draw and replicate those lines with much higher precision and control than was ever possible with my hands and multi-touch gestures.

This generative piece, with its multiple layers of crisscrossing lines, was almost a happy accident. It started as a generative checkered tablecloth in another generative piece, but when multiple such tablecloths accidentally got overlaid, more complex and intricate patterns emerged that deserved to be made into a standalone generative piece that I have called Swatch. This piece is a tribute to TwoToJazz, my original and long time playground for digital art.

11888.d:
I remember holding my breath and sitting on the bottom of the public pool where I spent most summers. Every so often I would hear a sound like breaking glass played by a transistor radio  and turn see the form of a diver plunging into the deep end. 

Consider the form of a diver seconds after they hit water. I am struck the grace of a freefall, the shock of transition from air to water, and the shedding of bits the old world carried with the skin. 

Formally this piece is also my attempt to blend a kind of lyrical figurativism with the technical and aesthetic demands of long-form token based generative art. In this piece, a randomized subset of digitally sculpted  forms are loaded, spatially transformed via heuristics and RNG, and then translated into simple animated particle systems. 

This process of transformation occurs a variable number of times, so each piece could contain the base form of anywhere between 1 and 10 divers.

this piece was created with threejs

I hope you feel the same as me that this is a very exciting piece coming out, a nod to Bauhaus architectural minimalism. In this piece I try to connect the concept of life and journeys to the animated paths, with the interpretation of the shapes representing important, critical elements of the path left to the viewer.  Without the critical events, we get the paths representing journeys, the threads of fate. 

Am I a forest person or city?  Some visualizations leave the viewer to ponder the question, while other iterations produce something more abstract in its setting.

The Strings of Fate in Greek Mythology.  The fabric of reality.
The paths represent the work of the three sisters of fate as they thread, prepared, and cut the strings of human destiny.  Some iterations have symbolic characters and line-shape interactions for the viewer to find and perhaps think of a meaning for themselves.

- 2 color themes: "moon" (white, gray, pale yellow) - 90%, "crimson" (deep red) - 10%

-----------------

Uses a custom top-down isometric rendering engine for building semi-realistic shadows. Pure JavaScript, no GPU required.

Works best in Chrome or Firefox on desktop. Safari on desktop and mobile browsers could be *extremely* slow.

Lower size will produce more artifacts in shadows, more pixelated look, but faster. Higher sizes produce smoother shadows, less visible pixels, but slower. The default buffer sizes are 1200x1200px.

You can also override the dimensions of a saved image file (pressing the 's' key) by adding `&savesize=2000` to the URL. Default is 2000x2000px.

Artwork is based on PNG layers (with masks), Disco Diffusion, python and p5.js code.

Vanilla javascript and some css on SVG from bitmap input.

Press "p" to download a 2000x2000 pixels png image (if"opened" in full page)
Press "s" to download a SVG image (if"opened" in full page)
Press "l" to load and use an image of yours (if"opened" in full page)

The most interesting aspect of this work is the use of some public domain artwork bitmap images as input dataset to generate a randomized grid of blended triangular surfaces.

Triangle is the basic shape from wich it's possible to construct all other shapes, at least on a finite discrete grid like our screens. How not to adore triangles blessing our screen?

The goal of this work is not trying to catch the "essential", the "vibe", or the "atmosphere" from an input artwork, neither to parasite it and shine with it's reflected light. The input images are a way to random noise, but you can use your own and  you'll see that Triagulatria's own caracter will be preserved and you'll have even more good time.


Note1: I tuned and selected different configurations of Triangulatria. Some of them in some cases may produce just a black square. It's a valid artistic outcome but I will reserve some mints to exchange them with the black ones, at my sole discretion (ask me for the change if you want it)

Note2: On some browsers (for example Firefox) some configuration in some cases may request a lot of computational effort for "painting" the SVG and the device may get stuck for long time. As the result is likely to happen, I decided to keep those configurations, waiting for technology to cope with actual limits. Sorry for the bad user experience.

The grid, from my point of view, is an archetype of Minimal Art, this works tends to bring disruption in this rectilinear/straight design.

____

This script use 18 different palettes to create a grid in its initial stage. Then it uses random positions and Perlin noise to copy and paste parts of the grid over the existing one. In this process, it could paste sample with different modes (source-over, screen, overlay, xor & difference) and different scale (downscaling the picked sample at different sizes).Each time the program repeats the operation, it reuses the changes it has previously made.

11994.d:
My journey with line art, discovering the state space of patterns created by simple lines lined up or crossing each other, started in late 2012, with developing a multi-touch iPad drawing/creativity app called TwoToJazz. What writing generative code since early 2022 has allowed me is to draw and replicate those lines with much higher precision and control than was ever possible with my hands and multi-touch gestures.

This generative piece, with its multiple layers of crisscrossing lines, was almost a happy accident. It started as a generative checkered tablecloth in another generative piece, but when multiple such tablecloths accidentally got overlaid, more complex and intricate patterns emerged that deserved to be made into a standalone generative piece that I have called Swatch. This piece is a tribute to TwoToJazz, my original and long time playground for digital art.

Press 's' to save an image.
